_about: Rows of the v2 hand test (PLAN-021 WP-G). Only what needs a person, a real model or this computer's own fonts; everything CI or tools/layout_check_script.py can measure is not here. Each row starts from a stated state, never from another row. A row is added in the same pull request as the fix it checks. {version} is read from metadata.txt when the bundle is built.

rows.title: Update in place, then untick and tick the plugin during a request
rows.starts_from: QGIS with the previous Cartogen AI version installed and a project open (any project)
rows.do: Follow 'Updating an existing install' in README_FIRST.txt to install 1_plugin/cartogen_ai_v{version}.zip over the installed one, restart QGIS twice, then send any short request (for example: how many layers are in the project?) and, while it runs, untick Cartogen AI in Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins > Installed and tick it again.
rows.expect: Help shows Version {version}; one toolbar button, one Plugins menu entry, one Cartogen panel; no red lines in the CartogenAI log tab; unticking during the request leaves no error and ticking again gives one button, one entry, one panel.
rows.evidence: Screenshot of the toolbar and Help after the update; the Log Messages CartogenAI tab saved as a text file

rows.title: Stop a long processing request; memory comes back
rows.starts_from: A new project with smoke_boundary and smoke_points loaded from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg
rows.do: Note QGIS's memory in the operating system's task manager. Send: Create 300000 random points inside smoke_boundary and add to each the distance to the nearest point of smoke_points. Press Stop in the panel after a few seconds. Watch the memory for a minute. Then send: how many layers are in the project?
rows.expect: The panel says it stopped; no output layer is added; memory does not stay high; the next request works.
rows.evidence: The memory figure before, at the peak and a minute after Stop (write the three numbers in the notes)
rows.needs: person and the operating system's task manager

rows.title: Undo of add_field: an empty new column goes, a filled one stays
rows.starts_from: A new project with smoke_points from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg
rows.do: Send: add a text field called notes to smoke_points. Then send: undo that. (Confirm the undo card.) Then send: add a text field called notes to smoke_points again, then: set notes to 'checked' for every feature, then: undo the last operation.
rows.expect: After the first undo the field notes is gone from the attribute table. After the second add and fill, undo does not remove it: the reply says the field now holds values and nothing was changed, and the values are still there.
rows.evidence: The evidence folders of the requests; a screenshot of the attribute table after each undo
rows.prompt: add a text field called notes to smoke_points
expected_tools.title: Contour lines of a loaded DEM do not start a download
expected_tools.starts_from: A new project with 3_test_files/smoke_dem.tif added as a raster layer (Layer > Add Layer > Add Raster Layer) and renamed to dem
expected_tools.do: Send: draw contour lines of the dem every 100
expected_tools.expect: A new line layer of contours appears (the reply names it and the file). The assistant does NOT call fetch_dem or run_steps (the evidence folder shows the tools). The reply says where the file is, and says so when it is in the temporary folder.
expected_tools.evidence: The evidence folder of the request; a screenshot of the Layers panel
expected_tools.prompt: draw contour lines of the dem every 100

expected_tools.title: 'animate the layer over time' runs the animation tool, not a how-to
expected_tools.starts_from: A new project with 3_test_files/smoke_events.csv added through Layer > Add Layer > Add Delimited Text Layer (X field lon, Y field lat, geometry point, CRS EPSG:4326)
expected_tools.do: Send: make the layer smoke_events temporal using the date field. Then, in the same chat, send: animate the layer over time
expected_tools.expect: The second request calls export_temporal_animation_frames and reports the frames it wrote; it does not answer with instructions for doing it by hand.
expected_tools.evidence: The evidence folder of the request

expected_tools.title: Elevation profile in a layout is added, not looked up again and again
expected_tools.starts_from: A new project with 3_test_files/smoke_dem.tif renamed to dem and smoke_roads from 3_test_files/smoke_network.gpkg; first send: create a print layout of the map called Test Layout
expected_tools.do: Send: Turn on elevation for the dem, then draw an elevation profile along the road in Test Layout
expected_tools.expect: The dem has elevation turned on and the layout holds an elevation profile item along the road. list_layout_items is called at most twice and fetch_dem is not called.
expected_tools.evidence: The evidence folder of the request; a screenshot of the layout
expected_tools.prompt: draw an elevation profile along the road

expected_tools.title: Charts linked to maps become layout charts, not an HTML dashboard
expected_tools.starts_from: A new project with smoke_admin from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg; first send: create a print layout of the map called Test Layout
expected_tools.do: Send: Produce charts linked to maps in Test Layout
expected_tools.expect: A chart item is added to the layout (add_layout_chart); no HTML dashboard is written.
expected_tools.evidence: The evidence folder of the request; a screenshot of the layout

expected_tools.title: 'Combine two layers into one' is a merge, not an imagery plan
expected_tools.starts_from: A new project with smoke_points and smoke_hubs from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg
expected_tools.do: Send: Combine the layers smoke_points and smoke_hubs into one layer.
expected_tools.expect: A merge runs and a merged layer is added. No satellite imagery search or feature extraction is started.
expected_tools.evidence: The evidence folder of the request
expected_tools.prompt: Combine the layers smoke_points and smoke_hubs into one layer

expected_tools.title: 'Convert to a raster with the population in each cell' is not a WorldPop plan
expected_tools.starts_from: A new project with smoke_admin from 3_test_files/smoke_data.gpkg
expected_tools.do: Send: Convert smoke_admin to a raster with the population in each cell.
expected_tools.expect: A rasterise algorithm runs on smoke_admin using its population field; fetch_worldpop_population is not called.
expected_tools.evidence: The evidence folder of the request
expected_tools.prompt: Convert smoke_admin to a raster with the population in each cell
